subject: MSA + Order Form redlines — IP, training opt-out, and feedback license
messages:
From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@sienna.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sienna Legal <legal@sienna.ai>, Elena Park <epark@sienna.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sienna redlines to MSA & Order Form — IP & model training

Avery — attaching our redlines to the standard MSA and the Order Form (Sienna_Redlines_MSA.pdf). High level: Sienna is not comfortable with broad training rights or any language that would allow Redwood to claim ownership over customer outputs or derivative products built from Sienna-generated content.

Key asks: 
- Explicit "Customer retains all rights to output" language in Section 3.
- No training of models on Sienna customer content without an opt-in agreement and separate commercial terms.
- Any telemetry used for quality/improvement must be stripped of customer-specific data, and Sienna needs an attestation about what is retained/hashed/anonymized.
- A narrow feedback license limited to safety and debugging (and not productization).

Please let us know whether Redwood can accept the above or propose alternative, narrow language. We're on a tight procurement timeline (target signature by 12/15).

Attached: Sienna_Redlines_MSA.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Marco Ruiz
Head of Legal & Compliance
Sienna AI

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@sienna.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Sienna Legal <legal@sienna.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sienna redlines to MSA & Order Form — IP & model training

Marco — thanks for the clear redlines and the timeline. We're aligned on wanting a clean commercial relationship and protecting your customer's outputs; there are a few tradeoffs to discuss on training and telemetry.

What Redwood can offer as a baseline: 
- Output ownership: add clause in Section 3 making explicit that Sienna (and its customers) retain ownership of outputs ("Customer Output" defined). Redwood will not assert ownership over Customer Output or derivatives created solely from Customer Output.
- Training opt-out: build an opt-out for "No Model Retraining on Customer Data" as an Order Form add-on. When opted-out, Redwood will not include Customer Content in model training pipelines. This will be a paid option (we'll propose pricing).
- Telemetry/feedback license: introduce a narrow, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use anonymized/aggregated telemetry and feedback for safety, quality, and security purposes. We will not use Customer Output for productization or commercial model training without explicit separate consent.
- Attestation & redaction: we can supply a data-retention and telemetry summary (what fields are logged, retention windows). We can commit to an attestation about PII handling and an option for longer-term retention under a specific add-on.

I'm attaching a first-pass response draft with proposed redline language (Redwood_MSA_response_draft.docx). Suggest we set a 30-minute legal roundtable this week so our counsel and yours can walk the exact text.

Can Ben and Grace be on the call? Ben can cover commercial impacts; Grace can speak to telemetry/audit capabilities. Proposed times: Fri 11/28 between 9-11am PT or Mon 12/1 afternoon.

Standby — we'll bake in conservative language until legal finalizes.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Director, Strategic Accounts (West)
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@sienna.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Sienna Legal <legal@sienna.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sienna redlines to MSA & Order Form — commercial tradeoffs

Quick note from the commercial side: Avery captured the right levers. If Sienna requires a full "no-training" covenant in the MSA/Order Form (i.e., Sienna data never used in any training pipeline), that materially changes the economics on our side — we typically provide a paid "Training Opt-Out" add-on to offset model maintenance and feature engineering costs.

Options we can propose now: 
- No-training add-on (monthly surcharge) that guarantees exclusion from training and extended telemetry deletion window.
- Standard agreement with a narrow anonymized-feedback license (no customer output used for product model training) — lower price.

If Sienna confirms the preferred path this week, I can push a revised Order Form and pricing sheet. We want to remain flexible but transparent about the cost of the guarantee.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Park <epark@sienna.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@sienna.ai>, Sienna Legal <legal@sienna.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sienna redlines to MSA & Order Form — follow-up and revised Order Form

Avery/Ben — thank you for the quick turnaround and the draft language. We reviewed Redwood_MSA_response_draft.docx and have two immediate asks before scheduling counsel-to-counsel: 

1) Auditability: Sienna needs an explicit audit log and explainability commitment for outputs used in any troubleshooting or security incident. Please confirm logs are available (and for how long) and whether we can request a forensic export.

2) Order Form: for procurement we need the Order Form reflect a firm commercial option for "No Model Retraining on Customer Data" (price and billing cadence), and a retention window for telemetry/usage logs. I've attached Sienna_revised_orderform_v2.pdf with our suggested commercial box checked.

Can Redwood confirm the retention window for production telemetry and whether KMS/HSM key management is available for Private deployments? This will determine whether we move forward with the add-on or accept the aggregate/anonymized approach.

Attached: Sienna_revised_orderform_v2.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Elena Park
Procurement Manager
Sienna AI

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <epark@sienna.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@sienna.ai>, Sienna Legal <legal@sienna.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sienna redlines to MSA & Order Form — telemetry, KMS, and next steps

Elena — quick operational answers to your asks: 
- Audit logs: production request/response telemetry is retained by default for 90 days in hosted deployments. We can extend retention under the Training Opt-Out add-on or with a dedicated retention SLA for Dedicated/Private customers. Exports for incident response are available; we'll coordinate an export process with Sienna security when needed.
- KMS/HSM: available for Redwood Private and Dedicated plans; we integrate with customer-managed KMS in major clouds. We can scope a KMS/IAM diagram for your security review.
- Forensic/Explainability: we can commit to providing request-level metadata and a summary of model inputs/outputs for debugging/security incidents; for full model-level explainability we'll need to scope the runbook and potentially an engagement fee.

Next steps: 
1) Redwood legal to table redline language based on the draft I circulated;
2) We can produce a revised Order Form that includes the Training Opt-Out pricing box for signature;
3) Proposed counsel call: Thu 12/3 10:00am PT — does that work for Sienna legal?

I'll coordinate internal owners and circulate the updated Order Form once legal confirms the language.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
